Quickstart Guide#

From the first opening to the first answer. Ten minutes, one route, no alternative: the variations and explanations are in the following chapters.

It only takes one thing to get started: the address of the console, which will have given you who installed it.

What you're about to do#

VibeCraft answers questions by quoting Your documents, not the general culture of a model. For it to succeed, the documents must first be uploaded and then indexed. There are five steps:

creare un progetto → caricare documenti → approvarli → costruire l'indice → chiedere

Create a Project#

Open the console. If you don't have a project yet, see "Welcome to VibeCraft. Choose the project you want to work on."

Premi New Project, give it a name, confirm.

The project is born empty: the badge at the top will read "Not indexed", and it is correct.

You do not choose where it ends up on disk: the location is decided by the server.

2. Upload two documents#

Go Into Intake from the top bar, or with Alt+1.

Drag files to the pane Drop files here. Markdown, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and others are fine: the conversion takes place on this machine, without sending anything out.

Two real documents of your domain are enough for the first round. Avoid huge files: the limit is 25 MB each.

3. Approve them#

The following documents do not automatically enter: they wait in a staging area. It is the revision, and it is used to prevent a badly converted file from entering the corpus.

In the right column, below 🗂️ To be reviewedAWARDS 🔎 Anteprima on a document.

Read the preview, not just the name - it's when you find out if the conversion made sense text. If you see red notices, the document has been converted from a fallback engine and may have lost tables and titles.

Se va bene: scegli una Categoria — per il primo giro 04 knowledge informative va benissimo — e premi ✅ ApproveRepeat for the second document.

4. Build the index#

Approve writes the files, but does not make them queryable yet. In the top bar, it has appeared Create index: press it.

The badge changes to 'Indexing in progress.' On a few documents, it takes minutes; on several dozen, much longer. You can switch sections in the meantime: when it finishes, you will receive a notification.

When the badge says «Ready index» you're fine.

5. Ask the first question#

Return to Console (Alt + 1). Write a real question, not a keyword: a full sentence gives the system more grip.

Premi Query the graph, or Ctrl + Enter.

The answer is written word by word. Open the tab Risposta to read it.

6. Read the sources — this is the step that counts#

Next to the answer, Citations this turn list the sections of the document that produced it, each with a score.

It's not a technical detail: it's the reason why this console is useful. The answer is a summary generated by a model, and he/she/it can make a mistake. The sources allow you to verify it in ten seconds.

If an answer surprises you, first look at where it comes from.

If that doesn't work,#

What do you seeIt almost always means
"no results" to every questionthe index has not been built, or it is empty
The document just uploaded does not appearapproved but not yet indexed: rebuild the index
the button does not start and a yellow warning appearsAn external service is off: report it to the person who manages the installation
«he did not answer, and it is correct»The system did not find enough material, and it tells you instead of making it up

The last case is not a failure, and it is the behavior that makes everything else reliable.

Where next?#

You have seen a third of the console. The rest, in order of usefulness:

  • Query the graph e Read the answer deeply — the search parameters, the map of relationships, how to understand why an answer came out that way;
  • Analyze the knowledge base — see the structure of what you have uploaded and estimate the impact of a change;
  • Bring documents into the project — generate documents with the template, import source code;
  • The Pipeline — to support a change from the first idea through to filing;
  • When something doesn't work — the complete diagnosis, beyond the four lines above.

They are the chapters of the complete user manual.

And if instead of knowing how do you do you want to understand what are you looking at — why the system chose those sources, when it refuses to answer, what does it really cost — there is The console at work: a real case followed from start to finish, with the numbers of a real installation.

How to Read This Manual#

1.1 Who is it for?#

This manual is for those usa The VibeCraft console: loads documents, queries the corpus, reads the graph, carries out a modification along the pipeline. It does not assume that you have installed the system or that you know how it is made inside.

It presupposes only one thing: that someone has already started the server and given you an address to open in the browser.

1.2 What you don't find here#

The manual stops where the interface ends. Three areas remain outside, and not by oversight:

ArgomentoWhere to look for it
Installation, hardware requirements, server startup, DockerREADME.md of the project, and the future Administrator manual
Environment variables, rag_config.yaml, selection of models, API keys, rolesAdministrator manual
HTTP endpoint, integration via MCP, command line usageSupplement manual
Interior architecture, design choices, safety arearag/README.md e rag/SECURITY_SURFACE.md

The rule that guided the writing: here it is explained what you see and what you decide, never how it is configured. Every time the text touches a configuration file or an environment variable, it stops and defers.

1.3 Conventions#

  • I names of the controls they appear in bold, with the exact interface label: Query the graph, Update index, ✅ Approve.
  • Gli section addresses they are written as paths: /intake, /pipeline, /analysis.
  • I file and folder names I am in monospaced font: docs/02_specs_normative/.
  • I interface messages They are in low quotation marks: «Index ready · to be updated».
  • Le limit notes They close the operational chapters. They are not mere warnings: they say what the function does not do, because finding out on your own takes time.

1.4 Screenshots#

The images are real captures from the console, not mockups, taken in the theme Classico on a window 1600 pixels wide, on the sample project Tetris. If your console looks different, the three most likely causes are: you are using the Matrix theme, the window is narrower and the layout has reorganized, or your version is newer than this manual.

Button labels are more reliable than images: if a screenshot and the text differ, follow the text and report the discrepancy.

1.5 Two honest premises#

The system can abstain. If there is not enough material in the corpus, the console does not make up an answer: it states it. Abstention is not a malfunction, and it is the behavior that makes everything else reliable. § 9.7 explains how to recognize it.

The system can get the order of the sources wrong. The retrieval of documents is a statistical estimate corrected by authority weights, not an exact search. The answer always cites sources precisely so that you can check them: the manual teaches you to read them, not to trust them blindly. This console speeds up the consultation of documents, it does not replace it.

2. What is VibeCraft Graph-RAG#

This chapter is meant to understand all the others. There are ten concepts: once understood, every screen of the console becomes readable without explanations.

2.1 The life cycle#

VibeCraft answers questions in natural language by citing the documents you have uploaded. The process is always the same:

documenti → indice → domanda → risposta con fonti → (eventuale) modifica progettata

Each step has its section in the console: Intake enter the documents, the button Update index makes them questionable, it Console accept the questions, Analisi show the structure of what you have uploaded, the Pipeline It accompanies a modification from the first interview until filing.

The point that distinguishes this system from a generic assistant: the answer does not come from the knowledge of the language model, but from your documents, and every statement is accompanied by the sources that produced it.

2.2 Project#

Un progetto It is the separation unit. It has its own folder that contains:

CartellaContenuto
docs/the searchable documents, divided into categories
code/the indexed source code, divided by scope
changes/the modifications in progress and their archive
database/the actual index, managed by the system

Documents, code, and index of one project never mix with those of another: a question posted in project A does not see project B. All projects, however, share the server, the models, and the external services.

There is a special project called legacy: it is from an installation prior to the separation by projects, kept for compatibility.

2.3 Document, category, section#

Un documento it is a Markdown file inside docs/, with at the head a block of metadata that declares its title, classification, and authoritativeness.

Le categorie there are six, and the choice is not aesthetic: it determines how the document will be weighted compared to the others.

CategoriaWhat goes there
00_meta_governanceglossaries, permission matrices, versioning policies, registers
01_architecture_normscoding standards, error contracts, testing strategies, interface directives
02_specs_normativethe actual functional specifications, with the rules
03_changes_historicalthe history of archived changes
04_knowledge_informativeinformational material: methodologies, notes, insights
05_project_specstechnological specifications of the project components

In the console you see them written as '00 meta governance', '01 architecture norms', and so on.

A document is not indexed as a whole: it is broken into sezioni (also called chunk), one for a second-level title, with a further division if the section is too long. It is the section, not the document, that is retrieved and cited.

2.4 Entities, code symbols, graph#

In addition to the text, the system extracts two types of nodes:

  • le entity — the domain terms declared in the documents, which become the shared vocabulary of the project;
  • i code symbols — classes, functions, endpoints, components, tables, services, extracted from the files below code/.

All this forms the knowledge graph: the nodes are documents, sections, entities, and symbols; the arcs are the relationships between them — a specification that inherits constraints from another, an entity referenced by a document, a function that implements a requirement.

The graph is the reason for the name Graph-RAG: when you ask a question, the system does not just retrieve the most similar sections, but follows the arcs to gather what is connected.

The REASONS pillars#

Each node is assigned to one of the seven pillars, which in the graph map determine the color:

CodicePilastroRaccoglie
REQRequirementsrequirements, specifications, use cases, scenarios
ENTEntitiesglossaries, data dictionaries, domain models, and all extracted entities
APPApproachmethodologies, strategies, approaches
STRStructurearchitecture, modules, schemes, diagrams
OPSOperationsworkflows, processes, state machines, pipelines
NRMNormsauthorizations, permits, policies, rules, compliance
SAFSafeguardssecurity, integrity, privacy, contracts, traceability

A node that does not fall into any of these appears as 'Unclassified', with the symbol —.

2.5 Authority and Scoring#

Not all sources carry the same weight. Every document has aauthority: a value that indicates how binding that source is. An authorization policy weighs more than an informational note, and a filed document weighs less than one in effect.

When you read the sources of an answer, each entry shows a score broken down into four contributions:

SiglaSignificato
Ddense — similarity of meaning between the question and the section
Ssparse — correspondence of the words actually used
CBColBERT — a finer comparison, word by word, applied to the best candidates
Aauthority — the weight of the source

A result with D tall and S Basso grasped the meaning without sharing the vocabulary; the opposite case indicates a literal correspondence. A Alto explains why a source has risen in the rankings despite not being the most similar.

2.6 Index, version, stale#

Theindice it is the questionable form of your documents. Until you build it, the files in docs/ They exist but no question finds them.

The index is versionato: every reconstruction produces a new version, which is activated only if it passes the quality checks. The previous version remains on disk, so rolling back is immediate. This mechanism is called blue/green, and for you it means only one thing: during a rebuild the console keeps responding with the old version, and you never see a halfway index.

An index is to be updated (stale) when the documents have changed after the last indexing. The console tells you this in the top bar; it is not an error, it is a reminder.

2.7 Job#

Long operations — indexing, document generation, refinement, project briefing — do not block the interface: they become job that run in the background and whose status is tracked by the console. You can change section while a job is in progress. When it finishes, a notification tells you.

2.8 The concepts of the pipeline#

They only concern the section Pipeline; if you are not planning changes, you can skip them.

  • Feature (or change): a modification in progress, with its own folder underneath changes/ which collects the documents produced throughout the five phases.
  • Type of development (dev type): the subfolder of code/ on which the modification insists — for example backend o frontend. It defines the technical context and the writing scope.
  • Contratto: the Canvas + Spec pair considered as a single whole. When you validate it, the system records quella version; if you then modify it, the console will notify you.
  • Validazione: the checks, partly automatic and partly entrusted to the model, that verify whether the contract is complete and consistent.
  • Open point: an issue left unresolved in the specification. It is not hidden: you must explicitly decide whether to accept it as it is or state how you resolved it, with a written justification.
  • Gate: the check that decides if the contract is in a condition to be passed to an agent who writes code.

2.9 What the system can't do#

  • He does not know what you have not uploaded. It does not draw on the Internet nor on the model's general knowledge. If the document is not in docs/, for the system it does not exist.
  • It does not guarantee that it will always find the right source. Retrieval is an estimate: it can put a related but not relevant section first. This is why the sources are always shown.
  • It does not verify the truth of the documents. If two rules contradict each other, the system applies the weights of authority, not common sense.
  • It does not delete approved documents and does not search across projects. Projects can be renamed (display name only) and deleted from the console; approved documents are removed on the filesystem. Each question stays in one project.
  • It remembers only a short thread, not conversations. The Console keeps a thread per project with the last 4 turns and passes the model only an excerpt of the previous answers: a long dialogue will not hold up. New thread clears it.

3. The interface: shell, navigation, status#

Everything described in this chapter remains on the screen regardless of which section you are using. Learning it once saves explanations in all subsequent chapters.

3.1 A single page, sections that remain in memory#

The console is a single-page application. When you switch from Console a Intake The browser does not reload anything: the section is loaded once and then kept in memory.

The practical consequence is good: returning to a section already visited is instantaneous, and what you were doing is not lost. A mid-pipeline interview, an answer already received, a document open for review remain where you left them.

The consequence to know: the console keeps the sections of in memory two projects at most. If you open a third one while the first two have ongoing operations, the message "Two projects have active operations. Wait for completion before opening a third project" appears. It is not a malfunction: it is the limit that prevents keeping an indefinite number of work sessions open.

3.2 The top bar#

From left to right:

ElementoFunzione
VibeCraft logoreturns to the project selection screen
Selettore Active projectchange project while staying in the current section
Index status badgesee § 3.3
Update indexappear only when there is something to do; see chap. 7
Section navigationsee § 3.4
Service badgecompare only if something does not respond; see § 3.5
Progettireturns to the project selection screen, from which you create or open a project; see chap. 4
Guidaopens the Guide page
Settingslanguage, theme, Rain effect and LLM models; see § 3.6

3.3 The index status badge#

It is the most important indicator on the console: it tells you if your questions will find anything.

TestoSignificato
"Unindexed"The documents are there but are not yet searchable
«Ready index»all set
"Indexing in progress"a reconstruction is in progress; the console continues to respond with the previous version
"Index error"The last construction has failed
‘Index to be reconstructed’the index is present but damaged or incomplete

To these are added two suffixes:

  • «· check…» — the console is still checking if the documents have changed. During the check, the refresh button does not appear, so as not to appear and disappear.
  • «· to be updated» — The documents have changed since the last indexing. You can continue to query: you will get answers based on the previous version.

The state updates itself every fifteen seconds.

3.4 Switching between sections#

The navigation has five work sections — Console, Intake, Pipeline, Analisi, Eval — and, detached on the right, the Guida, which is documentation of the architecture and not a place where one works.

The current section is highlighted. The browser's Back and Forward buttons work normally, and every link carries the active project with it: opening a section in a new tab does not make you lose the project.

If your installation is configured in read-only, three sections do not exist at all: Intake, Pipeline, and Eval respond with 'page not found.' They are not hidden out of caution, they are simply absent. See § 4.7.

3.5 When a service does not respond#

The console depends on two external services: Qdrant, which keeps the index, and Ollama, which runs the local language model. Every thirty seconds the console queries them.

If one of the two does not respond, a badge appears in the bar — for example 'Qdrant not reachable' — and hovering over it you can see the concrete effect:

  • Qdrant not reachable: queries and semantic map do not work.
  • Ollama not reachable: generation with the local model does not work.

The buttons that depend on the service being off they remain visible but do not start: by pressing them a warning appears «… not reachable: start it and try again». It is a deliberate choice — a button that disappears makes one believe that the function does not exist.

The rest continues to work: you can read the documents under review, scroll through the pipeline, consult the Guide.

3.6 Themes#

The theme is chosen in Settings (top right), under Interface, which offers Classico and Matrix. Both are dark; the difference is not in the brightness but in the effect:

TemaAspetto
Matrix (default)black and fluorescent green, with a rain of animated characters in the background and a scanning effect
Classicosober night blue, without rain or scanning

The images in this manual are on theme Classico: with the same content it remains more readable, because nothing moves behind the text. If your console does not look like the screenshots, this is the first thing to check — the default theme is the other one.

In the Matrix theme, a button appears 🌧 Rain on / 🌧 Rain off that stops the animation while maintaining the colors. The animation also respects the system setting for reducing motion; the button is used to reactivate it for those who have disabled it at the Windows level but want it here. In the Classic theme, the button does not appear, because there is no animation to stop.

The choice of theme is remembered between visits and is applied by the server to the first rendering of the page, so you do not see a flash of the wrong theme.

Also from Settings, under LLM models, you choose where the models run: all local (Ollama), all in the cloud, or per activity, with a provider and model for each. Among the providers there is also Claude Code, which uses the login of this machine without an API key. The API key is saved on the server and is never shown. The service badge reports Ollama only if it is the provider in use.

3.7 Keyboard shortcuts#

Alt + 1 … Alt + 6 they open the six navigation items in the order in which they appear:

TastiSezione
Alt + 1Console
Alt+1Intake
Alt + 3Pipeline
Alt + 4Analisi
Alt + 5Eval
Alt + 6Guida

They also work while you are typing inside a section. The other shortcuts are collected in Appendix B.

3.8 Notifications#

The messages appear at the bottom, one below the other, in four levels:

IconaLivelloQuando
ℹinformazioneneutral outcome
✓riuscitaThe operation was successful
⚠avvertimentothe operation hasn't started, or it started with reservations
✕erroreThe operation has failed

The first three disappear by themselves after five seconds. Errors remain until you close them: I am the only trace of what went wrong, and making them disappear would mean losing them while you look away.

3.9 Confirmation requests#

Some actions open a confirmation window within the page. Two have the danger variant, recognizable by the red border and button:

  • the launch of an agent in Agentic mode, which writes files to the disk (§ 12.7);
  • thearchiviazione of a feature, which is not reversible from the interface (§ 13.2).

When you see red, reread before confirming.

3.10 Narrow screens#

The layout reorganizes below 1100, 800, and 480 pixels in width: the navigation compresses and the side-by-side columns stack. All functions remain accessible, but screens with two panels — Console and Analysis — are inconvenient below 800 pixels, because the map and detail panel are no longer visible together.

Limits of this chapter#

  • The number of projects kept in memory is not configurable from the interface.
  • The services badge says se a service responds, doesn't it Why? He does not do it. The diagnosis is the responsibility of whoever manages the installation.
  • Alt shortcuts are not remappable.

4. Working with projects#

Everything in VibeCraft happens within a project. Before you can upload a document or ask a question, you must choose one.

4.1 The Welcome Screen#

When you open the console, if you haven't chosen a project yet, you will find the screen 'Welcome to VibeCraft. Choose the project to work on', divided into two columns: on the left the projects that already exist, on the right the ways to start a new one.

At first opening, the left column shows 'No project yet. Create a project or open an existing folder.'

4.2 Finding a project#

The projects are ordered by last opening, the most recent at the top: the memory of when you used them remains in your browser, so the order is personal and does not change for others.

The field Search for a project… filters the list by name or id as you type (a list filter, not corpus search). If none match, «No project matches the search» appears.

Each card shows four pieces of information:

ElementoWhat does he/she say?
Nomewhat did you name the project
Shortened paththe last two folders, for example …/projects/Tetris; the full path appears when you hover over it
Metadatinumber of documents, number of code files if there are any, date of last opening
Badgethe state of the index, with the same texts as § 3.3

A project without a path because it was inherited from a previous installation appears as 'Original Project'.

The counter at the top tells you how many projects you are viewing, taking the filter into account.

4.3 The “Start working” column#

Two actions, with a clear distinction:

  • New Project — "Create a new workspace." It creates an empty project.
  • Open project — "Connect an existing VibeCraft folder." Register in the console a project that already exists on disk but that the console knows nothing about.

Below, the memo that summarizes the model: 'Code, documents, and index remain separate for each project.'

Create a new project.#

Premi New Project: a window opens with a single field, Project name.

The note below the field explains where it will end up: "The folder is created in the directory managed by the server. You will be able to import code and documents from the Intake page."

Two things to know:

  • You don't choose the position on the disk — the server decides;
  • the project is created empty and not indexed. Immediately after creation, the badge will say «Not indexed», and this is correct: there is nothing to index yet. The natural path is to go to Intake (chap. 5) and then build the index (chap. 7).

4.5 Open an existing project#

Premi Open existing project: the window asks for a Project folder.

The folder must be a complete VibeCraft project, that is, it must contain a file project.yaml valid. If the console runs on your same machine, the button Browse folder opens the system selector. If it goes elsewhere the button does not appear, and the path must be typed manually, with two constraints noted for you: with a remote server only subfolders of the projects directory managed by the server are allowed, and in Docker the path mounted in the container is used.

4.6 Change Project#

From the selector Active project in the bar, or by returning to the home screen with Progetti or with the logo VibeCraft.

Changing project you stay in the same section: if you were in Analysis, see the Analysis of the new project. The work opened in the previous project remains in memory and you find it again by going back — within the limit of two projects of § 3.1.

4.7 Read-only mode#

An installation can be configured so that it does not allow changes. In that case:

  • On the home screen, the note 'Read-only mode: you can open already saved projects' appears;
  • the buttons New Project e Open project remain deactivated;
  • Intake, Pipeline and Eval do not exist: by writing its address you get 'page not found,' because those sections are simply not published.

The Console, Analysis, and Guide remain available: you can query and consult, not modify.

If you need to write and the console is read-only, the configuration must be changed by whoever administers the installation: it is not a user preference.

Limits of this chapter#

  • Projects can be renamed and deleted from the console. Rename changes only the display name (id, folder, and Qdrant namespaces stay unchanged). Deleting a managed root is a destroy (registry, tree, and Qdrant); for an external root it is an unregister (registry only; host files remain).
  • One does not search through multiple projects at the same time. The home/API filter (`?q=`) applies to the project list; every question lives within only one project.
  • There are no permits for the project. Those who reach the console see all registered projects; the separation is of data, not of access.
  • The order of recent projects is stored in your browser: on another machine, or after clearing the site data, it starts from scratch.

5. Bring documents into the project#

Section Intake (/intake) is the only gateway to knowledge. Whatever path you choose, one rule applies without exception: nothing arrives directly in docs/. Everything passes through a rest area called staging, where you look at it before accepting it. The review is chapter 6.

The page has four boxes: generate with the model, import files, import a code project, and review what has been entered.

5.1 Which of the three roads#

StradaWhen it is convenient
Generate with an LLMyou don't have the document and you want the model to write it, based on what the project already contains
Import documentsThe document already exists, in any office format
Import project from folderyou want to index source code, not documents

5.2 Generate with an LLM#

The model writes up to five Markdown documents, anchored to the already indexed content and the lessons from previous edits. Three fields:

  • Description of the development — what it should address. The more detailed it is, the less generic the result. If you leave it empty, the console responds 'Describe the development first.'
  • No. of documents — from 1 to 5.
  • Categoria docs/ target — one of the six from § 2.3.

Premi ▶ Start generation. The work starts in the background and the status progresses from «Job generation start…» to «Generation in progress (grounding + LLM)…». At the end, the console says «Generation completed» and reports how many documents were produced, how many were discarded, and the retrieval, generation, and total times.

It's minutes, not seconds. You can change sections: the work continues.

The documents end up in staging with the label generated. None of them reaches docs/ without your approval.

5.3 Importing documents#

Drag files to the pane 📎 Drag files here, or click to select them, or click it to open the selector.

The accepted formats are fifteen:

md · pdf · docx · pptx · xlsx · doc · xls · ppt · html · txt · csv · json · xml · epub · msg

Each file has a limit of 25 MBYou can drag more than one at the same time: they are loaded in parallel and each shows its own result.

The conversion takes place on this machine, without sending anything to external services. The original remains stored in staging; in docs/ Only the resulting Markdown is published.

5.4 Which Engine Converts What, and Why You Care#

FormatoMotoreWhat to expect
.mdnessunoenter native, no conversion
.pdfDoclingreconstructs tables and titles; uses optical recognition only on scanned pages. From a few seconds to a few minutes
.xlsx, .xlsdirect readingcells with coordinates and stored values, one sheet per section. The formulas are not recalculated; charts and images are excluded, with notice
.doc, .pptLibreOffice, then the engine of the modern formatlocal conversion, with macros and external links disabled
all the othersMarkItDowndirect conversion

After uploading, each file shows a badge with the engine actually used — which may not be the expected one, if the first attempt failed — and, when needed, a badge «⚠ N warnings: see preview».

The possible outcomes are three, and it is advisable to distinguish them:

EsitoWhat do you seeWhat does it mean
riuscitothe name of the engine, for example 'Native Markdown, no conversion'The file is in staging, ready for review
ripiego«MarkItDown as a fallback: Docling did not convert the file», plus the reason in fullThe file is in staging, but converted by a less accurate engine: tables and titles are not reconstructed in a verified way
fallitoin red, "Conversion failed: check the document's format, protection, and text"the file It won't go in. in staging

Fallback is the tricky case, because the document exists and seems fine. It happens when the expected converter is not installed or fails: typically with PDFs, when Docling templates are missing, and with DOC and PPT, when LibreOffice is missing.

The warnings deserve attention: a poorly scanned PDF or a spreadsheet full of formulas can produce poor Markdown. The preview of chapter 6 serves exactly this purpose.

The actual availability of the converters depends on how the installation was set up: LibreOffice and the Docling templates are optional components. If a format in the list fails on your machine, it is a matter of installation, not usage.

5.5 Importing a draft code#

It is used to index the source code, so that the responses can reference functions, classes, and endpoints in addition to the documents.

Three fields:

  • Absolute path of the source project — the folder to copy. The button 📁 Browse… opens the system selector, and is only available if the console is running on your machine.
  • Target in code/ — the target scope. They are the same scopes as in the «Development Type» dropdown in the Pipeline. If none exist, the dropdown says: «(no scope in code/: create one)».
  • New field con Aggiungi — to create one on the fly.

The procedure has two stages, and the second is not available until you have completed the first.

5.6 The Import Preview#

🔍 Preview calculate what would happen, without writing anything. Also state in which of the two ways you would move:

  • bootstrap — the destination folder is empty: everything that can be copied is copied;
  • additivo — the folder is already populated: only new files are copied.

The result is a row of four badges:

BadgeSignificato
N newfiles that would be copied
Identical Nfiles already present and identical: skipped
In conflictsfiles already present but diversi
N excludednon-copyable files (binaries, ignored folders)

Below, the expandable lists of conflicts, new and excluded.

The rule that counts, and that the console writes in red when there are conflicts: Conflicts will NEVER be applied, existing files remain intact. The import is additive. If you need to overwrite something, you do it outside the console.

If you change the path or scope after the preview, the plan is invalidated and ▶ Apply returns deactivated: a plan calculated on other data does not apply.

5.7 Apply, and project brief#

▶ Apply executes the plan: the system says "Application in progress (backup + copy + reindex)...". At the end, you see how many files were copied and where the backup folder is — or "none (empty folder)" if the destination was empty and there was nothing to save.

Below, the box 🧭 Project brief generates an architectural summary of the imported project, anchored to the graph. The dropdown lists the imports that have already succeeded, including from previous sessions.

The brief it is not a privileged document: enter staging like everyone else, with the label brief, and it must be approved.

5.8 Read Only#

If the installation is read-only, this section does not exist: the address /intake responds 'page not found.' See § 4.7.

Limits of this chapter#

  • It does not overwrite. Neither documents already approved, nor files in conflict during code import.
  • It cannot be deleted from the console. A document approved by mistake is removed from the filesystem, not from the interface.
  • The quality of the conversion is not guaranteed. A scanned PDF produces what the OCR is able to read. Checking the preview is not a formality.
  • The spreadsheet formulas are not being recalculated: the stored value is read. A sheet saved without calculated values produces empty cells.
  • The generation and the brief require a reachable model: Ollama locally (the default) or the provider chosen in Settings. With the service off, the buttons remain visible but give a warning and do not start (§ 3.5).
  • After the approvals, the index does not update automatically: you have to press Update index in the top bar (chap. 7).

6. Review and approve#

The box 🗂️ To be reviewed It is in the right column of the Intake page and remains visible while you scroll. It is the point where you decide what really goes into the corpus.

6.1 Why staging exists#

An indexed document changes the answers. If it ended up in docs/ Without control, a poorly converted PDF or an approximate generated text would start competing in the ranking with the real standards, and you would discover it weeks later from a wrong answer.

Staging is a staging area: the document exists, you can read it, but it is not yet queryable. The instruction at the top of the box summarizes the path: 'Approve to write in docs/ or reject (remains tracked). Once the approvals are finished, press Update index in the top bar.

6.2 The list#

The counter shows how many documents are waiting. ↻ Reload update the list. If there is nothing, read 'Nothing in staging'.

Each entry carries an origin badge:

BadgeWhere does it come from
importeda file that you uploaded (§ 5.3)
generatedwritten by the model (§ 5.2)
briefthe architectural synthesis of an imported project (§ 5.7)

Next to it, the file name, the conversion engine, and the date. 🔎 Anteprima opens the detail.

6.3 The detail panel#

It opens under the selected item and has two parts: the information about the conversion and the rendered document.

The conversion information may contain:

VoceWhat does he/she say?
Conversionewhich engine was actually used
Original and SHA-256the name of the starting file and its fingerprint, abbreviated, with the full value in the tooltip. The original remains in staging and is not published
Normalizzazionefor legacy formats: from which format to which, with which tool, locally and with macros disabled
PDFhow many pages, how many without selectable text, if optical recognition has been used
⚠ Reason for fallbackbecause the intended engine was not used
List of avvisiwhat the conversion has lost or could not handle
Previous approval errorif an attempt has failed: when, why, and the confirmation that nothing has been published

Below, the preview of the Markdown as it will be indexed — with the tables rendered, in the case of spreadsheets.

Read the preview, not just the badges. It's the moment when you discover that a PDF has produced a column of broken words or that a spreadsheet is full of empty cells.

6.4 Refine with template#

✨ Refine with LLM rewrites the document in staging in a more orderly form. After the first pass the button becomes Refine again and the title carries the 'refined' badge.

The operation starts in the background: 'Refinement started: it may take a few minutes...'. The model is required.

Refinement improves form. Does not verify the content and it cannot recover what the conversion has lost: if the original was unreadable, the result will be tidy and still wrong.

6.5 Approve#

Two fields, below the preview:

  • Categoria docs/ — where it will end up. It is not a formal classification: it determines the weight of the document in the ranking (§ 2.3 and § 2.5). An informational note placed among the rules will count as a rule.
  • File name — automatically suggested based on the original name, in lowercase and with hyphens. You can change it.

The board remembers what it publishes: "By approving, in docs/<categoria>/ only the file is written .md shown here, with the governance frontmatter.

Premi ✅ Approve. During writing, the button locks, because a double click would produce two writings. At the end, read:

Approved → docs/<categoria>/<file>. Approve the other files, then click «Update index».

The file is never overwritten: if a document with that name already exists, the approval fails and tells you, without publishing anything.

6.6 Reject#

The field Reason (refusal) and the button 🚫 Refuse. The reason is needed: the document is not deleted, it is moved among the rejected ones and the reason remains written next to it. In a month, it will explain why that file is not in the corpus.

6.7 And then the index#

Approve writes the file, but does not make it queryable. As soon as you finish, the badge in the bar changes to 'Index ready · to be updated' and appears Update index. Chapter 7 explains what happens when you press it.

It is advisable to approve everything you have pending and then update only once.

Limits of this chapter#

  • Approve is not canceled from the interface. A document published by mistake must be removed from the filesystem.
  • The text in staging is not modified from the console. You can refine it with the model or reject it and reload a corrected version, but there is no editor.
  • The file name and category do not change after approval.
  • Refining requires a model and it can last minutes.
  • A rejected document stays on the disk. It is not a cancellation, it is a filing with a reason.

7. Index and keep the index up to date#

As long as the index does not exist, the documents in docs/ They are just files: no query can find them. Building it is the operation that makes them queryable. It is done from a single button, in the top bar.

7.1 Creating the index the first time#

In a newly created project the badge says «Not indexed» and the button is called Create index.

Press it after approving the first documents. The badge changes to 'Indexing in progress' and the button to 'Indexing...', disabled.

The first construction is the slowest: the system must read each document, divide it into sections, calculate its numerical representation, and build the graph. On a corpus of a few dozen documents, it takes minutes.

You can continue working: switch sections, read the Guide, prepare other documents.

7.2 When to rebuild#

The badge tells you by itself. After you have approved a document or imported some code, it becomes "Index ready · to be updated" and the button reappears, this time as Update index.

It is not urgent: you can continue querying and you will get correct answers, but based on the documents as they were at the last indexing. The new material simply does not appear.

Update when you have finished a block of approvals, not after each individual file: the reconstruction costs the same.

If the badge says ‘Index to be reconstructed’ the situation is different: the index is present but incomplete or damaged, and the button becomes Rebuild index. Here it is advisable to act immediately.

The suffix «· check…» It means that the console is still comparing the documents with the latest version of the index. During the check, the button does not appear: this is intentional, so as not to show a command that might prove to be useless.

7.3 What happens during the upgrade#

The update is incrementale: only the changed documents are reprocessed. The console checks the progress every few seconds and updates the badge.

In the meantime, the previous version of the index remains active. You never see an index halfway: the questions continue to work and return consistent results, simply not yet updated.

If you launch an update while another one is in progress, the request is neither lost nor duplicated: it is queued, and multiple pending requests are merged into a single one.

7.4 Versions and Exchange#

Every construction produces a new version of the index, which is put into service only after passing quality checks. The swap is instantaneous and the previous version remains on disk.

The number of versions retained is a choice of the installation, and determines how far back you can go. Rolling back to a previous version is not commanded from the console: it is an administrator operation.

7.5 How it ends, and what it means#

At the end a notification appears, preceded by project name — «demo manual: Updated index.» — because you may have launched the update on one project and in the meantime moved to another. There are four possible outcomes:

MessaggioSignificatoWhat to do
«Updated index.»everything in place, the new version is in serviceniente
«Index built but not activated: quality checks not passed.»The new version was rejected because it worsened the quality of the answersThe previous version remains in service. It is a guardrail that has worked: it is worth understanding which document worsened the recovery (chap. 14)
Index built but not loaded. Try again.The construction succeeded but the loading did notrepeat the update
«Indexing interrupted.»The work stopped before the endrepeat; if it repeats, it is a problem to report

The second case is the one that surprises the most: the indexing went well and however, the index has not changed. It is the intended behavior — better an old index that works than a new one that performs worse.

If the badge stays on 'Index Error,' the last build has completely failed and the error notification, which does not disappear on its own, indicates why.

7.6 Automatic updating after archiving#

There is a case in which you do not have to press anything: closing an edit in the Pipeline (§ 13.2) archives the documents and automatically triggers a complete re-indexing. At the end, if you have given permission to the browser, you also receive a system notification — useful because it is the longest operation of the entire workflow and no one stays to watch the screen.

Limits of this chapter#

  • Indexing does not start by itself when you approve a document. It's a choice: you accumulate the work and update all at once.
  • A part of the project is not indexed. The command is one and it applies to everything.
  • You cannot cancel an update in progress from the interface.
  • The return to a previous version is not exposed in the console.
  • Qdrant needs to be running. With the service turned off, the button signals and does not start (§ 3.5).

8. Interrogate the graph#

La Console (/) is the section where the most work is done. On the left, one asks, on the right, one reads.

8.1 The two columns#

The vertical line between the two panels can be dragged to widen either one: the tooltip says 'Drag or use ← / → to resize.' It is also keyboard-accessible — you reach it with the Tab key and move it with the arrow keys, Home, and End.

The chosen width is remembered in your browser, so you set it only once.

8.2 Write the question#

The field Domanda he/she suggests the form with an example: «Ex. What events are planned in June?». It widens as you write.

You can send with the button or with Ctrl + Enter, which is faster when you are doing many of them in a row.

8.3 Advanced options#

Under the field, the collapsible voice Advanced options It displays two adjustments.

Results to retrieve (from 1 to 20, usually 5). How many document sections does the system retrieve before composing the answer.

  • Raising it helps with broad questions, which touch on multiple documents.
  • Raising it too much makes it worse: marginal material enters, the response is diluted, and timing increases.

Depth in the graph (from 0 to 5, normally 2). How many steps the system takes along the relationships, starting from the found documents.

  • A 0 no expansion: only what resembles the question.
  • A 1-2 Documents directly connected come in — the inherited constraints, the referenced glossary. It is the most common useful case.
  • Furthermore, the context expands rapidly and brings in material unrelated to the question.

If the answer seems poor to you, try increasing the depth first; if it seems confusing, reduce the number of results.

8.4 Interrogate#

Query the graph start. During processing, three dots appear and a seconds counter: it is used to distinguish a slow query from a frozen console.

The badge in the top right follows four states:

BadgeSignificato
Waitingno questions asked yet
Processing…in progress
Response receivedcompletata
ErroreSomething went wrong; the detail is in the notification

The button depends on Qdrant: with the service off it warns and does not start (§ 3.5).

8.5 The Self-Written Answer#

The answer appears word for word, while the model produces it. It's not a visual effect: you can start reading before it finishes, and immediately notice if it is taking a wrong direction.

At startup, the console shows the panel Graph map; to read the text, go to the tab Risposta.

8.6 Read sources#

Next to the answer, the box Citations this turn List the sections that produced it. For each: the document, a score, a proportional bar, and four contributions. Below, Accumulated citations gathers the documents cited along the thread: in the left column, under the question, the Thread card keeps the last 4 turns of the project (no more than 24 cited documents), New thread clears it, and if the index has changed since the last turn it warns that earlier answers may be stale.

SiglaWhat does it measureHow to read it
Dsimilarity of meaningtall with S low: he grasped the meaning without sharing the words
Scorrespondence of wordstall with D low: literal coincidence, perhaps accidental
CBend comparison, word for wordconfirm or resize the first two
Aauthority of the sourcehigh: the source has risen because it is binding, not because it resembled more

This is the point at which the console can be controlled. If the answer surprises you, look at the sources before believing or dismissing them: very often the surprise can be explained by a document you did not expect in the ranking.

8.7 How long did it take#

Next to the answer, the total time in seconds appears. It varies a lot: a question asked recently can come back almost instantly, because the answers are stored until the index changes. After an index update, the times return to the full ones.

8.8 “Project Status”#

At the bottom of the left column, six updatable rows with ↻:

RigaWhat does he/she say?
recallthe measured quality of recovery, in percentage, with the trend compared to previous measurements. Green above the threshold, red below. Leads to the Eval section
Grafohow many nodes and how many edges. Go to the Analysis section
Indexed sectionshow many units of text are queryable
Index versionwhich version is in service, and whether it is 'up to date' or 'needs updating'
Qdrantreachable or not
Ollamareachable or not

If 'Indexed Sections' is set to zero, no question will work: the index is missing (chap. 7).

8.9 Writing questions that work#

The system looks for similarity of meaning with the text of your documents. Some useful habits arise from this:

  • Use the project's vocabulary. The glossary terms are nodes of the graph: naming them leads straight to the right material.
  • One question at a time. Three questions in one produce an answer that deals well with one of them.
  • Ask for things that the documents can contain. «How many points is a cleared row worth?» works; «is it a good idea?» no, because no document contains that judgment.
  • You prefer the full question to the keywords. It is not a search engine: a whole sentence gives more leads than two nouns.

8.10 When the system does not respond#

It can happen, and it is expected. If there is not enough material in the corpus, the console abstains instead of making things up: the answer says that the information is not there.

When the abstention is also formally declared, the ballot JSON Response riporta «abstained — did not respond, and it is correct». It does not always happen: the rejection can arrive as a normal text, with the outcome recorded as success. For you it changes little — you read anyway that the information is not there — but if someone builds an automation on the responses, it is a distinction that they need (§ 9.7).

An abstention means one of three things: the document was not uploaded, it was not indexed after uploading, or the query uses words too different from how the issue is written in the documents. § 9.7 helps to distinguish the cases.

Limits of this chapter#

  • There is only a short thread. The model sees an excerpt of the last turns of the project thread (4 at most), not the whole dialogue.
  • There is no history of questions. By reloading the page, the response is lost.
  • One no longer questions more than one project together.
  • Saved answers are not cleared from the interface: the same question returns immediately until the index changes.
  • Recovery is an estimate. The right source may not be the first, and with a low number of results it may be left out.

9. Read the answer in depth#

The right column of the Console has four tabs. The first gives the answer; the other three are used to understand where does it come from, and they are what distinguish this console from any ordinary assistant.

SchedaWhat is it for
Rispostathe text, with the sources (chap. 8)
Graph mapthe relationships between the documents involved
Prompt contextthe exact text sent to the model
JSON Responsethe complete diagnostics

It is active when opened Graph map, not Answer.

9.1 The map: two or three dimensions#

The map starts in 3D, navigable with the mouse: drag to rotate, scroll wheel to zoom, right-click to move, click on a node for details.

The toggle 2D / 3D switch to the flat view, more suitable for reading labels and taking a shot.

Three-dimensionality is not decorative: the flat view can handle a few hundred nodes, beyond which it becomes a tangle and slows down the page; the three-dimensional one can support knowledge bases of tens of thousands of nodes.

The button of adattamento Bring everything back into the frame when you have lost track.

The arrangement of the knots it is not stable: the same question asked twice produces different layouts. Trust the colors, the shapes, and the legend, not the positions.

9.2 The colours#

The legend REASONS Pillars associate a color with each of the seven pillars of § 2.4. The shapes distinguish the type: ▢ Document, ◯ Entity.

Color answers only one question, but an important one: What is the nature of the material on which this answer is based? An answer built almost entirely on nodes Norms e Safeguards it has a different weight from one built on nodes Approach: the first rests on constraints, the second on methodological guidelines.

Which color corresponds to which pillar is indicated by the legend, not this manual: the colors are defined by the theme and change between Classic and Matrix.

9.3 The details of a node#

By clicking a node, a panel opens with name, type, pillar, classification, description, and the list Connessioni — every relationship with its direction and its type. It ends with ×.

Next to the node counter, a button alternates between Show all N nodes e Only the immediate neighbors. The contextual map starts from the documents found and their immediate neighbors: just a step away, a typical question touches about six hundred of them, unreadable.

9.4 Contextual or complete#

PulsanteMostra
Contextual graph (default)only what contributed to the last answer
View full graphthe entire knowledge base, with the badge Global view
Contextual Graphreturn to the graph of the last query

The complete graph is used to explore, not to verify an answer.

9.5 Before the first question#

Without queries the map invites: 'The contextual graph will appear after the first query, or click View full graph to explore the entire knowledge base." Below, three clickable example questions:

  • What documents exist in the corpus?
  • Which domain entities exist?
  • What are the main requirements?

I am a good test after the first indexing: they respond from the graph, so they also work with Ollama turned off.

If the graph does not load, 'Unable to load the graph' appears with the details and a button Riprova.

9.6 The context of the prompt#

The card shows the exact text sent to the model, with the character count.

It is the card that resolves discussions. If the answer ignored a document you thought was relevant, here you can see if that document was in the context: if it is not there, the problem is in retrieval (increase the results or depth); if it is there and was ignored, the problem is in generation.

9.7 The technical outcome#

The card JSON Response — titled «RAG Response Inspection» — opens with a badge that declares how it went:

BadgeSignificatoWhat to do
success — risposta generatacomplete path: recovery plus modelniente
graph_answer — risposta dal grafostructural question, direct answer from the graph without a model. It is the fastest and most verifiableniente
abstained — non ha risposto, ed è correttoinsufficient material, and the system said socheck that the document is uploaded and indexed; rephrase with the project's vocabulary
no_results — nulla di pertinente in indicethe recovery found nothingas above; check that 'Indexed Sections' is not zero
no_graph_nodes — trovato in Qdrant, assente nel grafoThe text is there but it has no relationshipsoften means a document without declared entities

Next to it, the time taken.

None of these is a failure. Abstention is the system that does its job.

A warning about the first and the third. The outcome abstained requires the model to declare abstention in an agreed-upon form; if it refuses by writing it in plain prose, the outcome remains success even though the text is a rejection. Read the answer, not just the badge. The difference matters especially for those who consume the answers from a program.

9.8 The two columns of diagnostics#

On the left, how the context was built:

  • Semantic Retrieval · Qdrant — the recovered sections with their scores;
  • Graph Expansion · NetworkX — the starting nodes and how many nodes and edges have been added following the relationships;
  • Raw JSON Data · RAG — the complete response from the server.

On the right, the generated response.

The comparison between the first two entries shows which mechanism did the work: many expanded nodes means that the answer owes more to the graph than to textual similarity.

9.9 When to Use Raw JSON#

Practically never, in normal use. It's needed when you have to report strange behavior to the system maintainer: it contains section identifiers, the index version, and complete scores, that is, everything necessary to reproduce the case.

9.10 Moving Between Keyboard Boards#

The tab bar is navigated with the arrows ← e →; Home e Fine They lead to the first and the last. Only one card at a time enters the tabulator sequence, so with Tab you exit the bar instead of going through it all.

Comparing the answer with the context sent to the model — that is, switching between the first and the third tab — is the operation that is done most often when an answer is not convincing, and from the keyboard it costs two keys.

Limits of this chapter#

  • The layout of the graph is not reproducible.
  • The contextual map refers to the last query: a new question replaces it.
  • The complete graph is heavy on large bases; the flat view may not support it.
  • Neither the map nor the context is exported from the interface.
  • The four tabs empty when the page is reloaded.

10. Analyze the knowledge base#

Section Analisi (/analysis) looks at the corpus from above, without asking questions. Answers questions different from those of the Console: What is what I uploaded made of? Where does it resemble? What breaks if I touch this?

Two panels: the semantic map on the left, the node inspector on the right.

10.1 The semantic map#

Each point is a sezione of the document, placed near sections of similar meaning. The proximity is calculated based on content, not on the folder: two sections of different documents dealing with the same thing end up next to each other.

At the top, the status line says how many sections, of how many documents, and how many similar pairs. ↻ Reload ricalcola.

10.2 Colours and rings#

Il colore It is the group: documents that mention the same entities receive the same color. They are the thematic communities of the corpus, inferred from the content.

Thewhite ring marks the bridge documents: those who connect otherwise separate groups. They deserve attention — a glossary, a transversal specification, a standard that everyone inherits. If a bridge document changes, the effect spreads far.

10.3 Exploring#

Hovering over a point shows the name. Clicking it selects it, and the inspector on the right gets populated. The legend lists the groups.

10.4 The twin sections#

Under the map, the panel «Very similar sections in different documents» List the almost identical pairs. Clicking on a row, the map highlights the two points and the line that connects them.

It is the most useful panel for the maintenance of the corpus. A similar pair is almost always one of these three cases:

  • duplicazione — the same content written twice. The two copies compete for ranking and, when they diverge, no one knows which one is valid;
  • legitimate repetition — a rule referred to in a document that inherits it;
  • supporting text — headings and premises are the same, which mean nothing.

It is worth scrolling through it after each substantial import.

10.5 The selected node#

The field Search for a node: document, entity, or code it suggests names while you type; Mostra It opens it. You can also get there by clicking a point on the map.

The list Relazioni It shows all the links, and each entry is clickable: you move from node to node following the relationships, which is the fastest way to understand how a document is connected.

10.6 Potential impact#

Below, Potential impact draws in concentric rings what is reachable from the selected node. The node is at the center; the first ring is what touches it directly, the second what touches the first, and so on. The Depth selector goes from 1 to 4. A ring is a distance in the graph, not a confirmed effect: that is why the title says potential.

The legend distinguishes document, entity and code. Tooltips and clicks work as on the map.

The stroke of each edge shows the kind of relation, and a second legend explains it: solid for structural (taken from a file or a parser), dashed for curated (declared in frontmatter, not a certification), dotted for inferred (an algorithm's guess, like the IMPLEMENTS edges between code and sections), dash-dot for unspecified (an older graph that does not record it: not a verification). Below the legend, the edge list shows kind, weight and reliability for each edge when the graph has them. Weight and reliability are not calibrated probabilities, and an inferred edge stays inferred even with a high score. A structural edge at the end of a path does not verify the whole path.

10.7 The most rewarding use#

Before opening a change in the Pipeline, search here for the document or the symbol you are about to touch and look at the potential impact at depth 2 or 3.

In a few seconds you see which specifications constrain it, which entities are involved, and which code implements it. It is a check that takes a minute and often changes the scope of the modification — particularly when you discover that the node you were about to touch has a white ring.

Limits of this chapter#

  • The position of the points is a projection. Many dimensions squashed into two: roughly faithful proximities, precise distances no. Do not measure on the map.
  • The groups are not an official classification: they are derived from the entities mentioned and change with each reconstruction of the index.
  • «Similar» does not mean «duplicate». The list highlights candidates, the evaluation is yours.
  • The propagation follows the relations recorded in the graph: those declared in the documents, those taken from parsers and those inferred from code. An unwritten connection does not appear, and an inferred edge stays a guess.
  • The map reflects the latest indexing, not the documents just approved.
  • Qdrant needs to be running.

11. The Pipeline: Setup, Explore, Canvas#

La Pipeline (/pipeline) accompanies a modification from the initial idea up to archiving. It does not write code for you: it builds the contratto that says what needs to be done and why, and does so by anchoring each step to the documents already in the corpus.

If your job is to review documents and not design changes, you can skip chapters 11, 12, and 13.

11.1 The five stages#

#FaseProduce
1Explore — Interview requirementsexplore.md
2Canvas — REASONS Canvascanvas.md
3Propose — Spec + Final promptspec.md and the prompt for the agent
4Drift — Check misalignmentthe relationship between contract and real code
5Archivia — Archive + Re-indexthe archived modification and the rebuilt index

The stepper above displays all five, each with its own state: not generated, in progress, completed, with warnings, failed. The stages can be revisited by clicking on them, but You don't skip the order: each phase needs the document approved by the previous one.

11.2 Name the change#

The field Feature name in the left column identify the work and give the name to the folder below changes/. Load / Resume opens an existing edit and takes you back to the last stage that produced something — but it brings back the documenti, not the conversation from the interview (§ 11.6).

Choose a descriptive and stable name: it will appear in the final prompt, in the archive, and, after archiving, in the quality measurement of chapter 14.

11.3 Local drafts#

The console writes "Drafts saved only in this browser," and it should be taken literally. While you work, the text is stored locally; if you reload the page or come back the next day, two buttons appear:

  • Restore local draft — takes up again what you had written;
  • Discard draft and use server file — throws away the local copy and starts again from the saved files.

There are two consequences, and it is wise to know them beforehand: the draft does not follow you to another computer, and it disappears if you clear the site data. Until you press Save changes, the server knows nothing about what you wrote.

11.4 The type of development#

The curtain Type of development chooses the subfolder of code/ interested — for example backend o frontend. The field New type of development con Aggiungi creates one.

As the note says, "determines in which subfolder of code/ The generated files will be written, upstream of the entire pipeline. It's not a label: it defines the writing perimeter of the phase 3 agent. Choose it before starting, because changing it afterwards invalidates the technical context collected up to that point.

11.5 Checking files#

The card Generated file check it shows at a glance which of the three documents exist. Before uploading a feature it displays «Upload a feature to see the file status».

11.6 Phase 1 — The Interview#

The first phase is an interview: an interviewer asks you questions about the functionality, and from your answers arises explore.md.

If you haven't started yet, the console shows three steps with their status:

  1. Give a name to the feature
  2. Choose the type of development
  3. Describe what you want to build, below

Write in the field Response to the AI Tech Lead and sends, also with Ctrl + Enter. The conversation accumulates in bubbles.

It is worth responding at length. The ambiguities you leave here become open points in phase 3, and at that point you will have to decide them in writing. Better to dissolve them now, or leave them on purpose knowing they will come back.

Questions the documents already answer#

Before asking you a question, the interviewer looks it up in the project's indexed documents. Each reply comes in three blocks:

  • Già documentato (already documented): questions the documents already answer. You see the answer with its source (document § section) and do not need to reply. If the answer is wrong, fix the document, not the interview: otherwise you end up with two different specifications;
  • Da decidere: i documenti non concordano (to decide: the documents disagree): two documents give incompatible answers. You see the options A, B… each with its source and authority class, and you choose;
  • Domande aperte (open questions): what the documents do not say. These are the only ones to answer.

An answer is listed as already documented only if the system finds, in the cited section, the sentence given as evidence; otherwise the question stays open. If the project is not indexed or search is unavailable, the interview carries on and says so with «⚠ Documentazione non consultata»: in that case no question was checked against the documents. All the text, sources included, goes into explore.md and from there into the Canvas.

The conversation does not reload from the server#

It is the point that surprises the most, and it is useful to know it before closing a tab.

The back-and-forth with the interviewer lives only in your browser. The server receives the interview text only once, when you press Finish and generate explore.md, and from that moment it keeps the document — not the conversation.

Three practical consequences follow from this:

  • premendo Load / Resume on an already completed feature the chat box it appears empty, even though the interview took place: what you find is explore.md in the review box below;
  • the conversation survives a page reload only through the local draft (§ 11.3), and only in the same browser;
  • if you change computers, or delete the site's data, the interview is lost — meanwhile explore.md, if you generated it, stay.

From here a simple rule: do not leave an interview halfway hoping to resume it elsewhere. If you need to interrupt yourself, press Finish and generate explore.md even on an incomplete interview: the document can be corrected by hand in the editor, a lost conversation cannot.

11.7 Close the interview#

Finish and generate explore.md closes the interview and produces the document. The box appears Revision · explore.md, with the notice «Approve before continuing»: an editor with the text, Save changes to rewrite it on the server, and ✅ Approve → go to Canvas.

The editor is at your disposal: the text produced by the model is a draft, not a report.

11.8 Phase 2 — The Dry-run#

Before generating the Canvas, 🔎 Dry-run mostra which sources would he/she use, with their scores, without spending a token.

It is the most convenient check of the entire pipeline. In a few seconds you can see if the system is about to build the Canvas based on the right specifications. If the sources are missing the document that regulates the area you are touching, the problem is upstream — that document is not indexed, or the interview did not use its vocabulary — and generating now would produce a Canvas anchored to the wrong material.

Always do it. It costs nothing.

11.9 Generating the Canvas#

Generate Canvas start the production: «Canvas generation in progress via local LLM…». It is an operation of minutes.

The REASONS Canvas organizes the change according to the seven pillars of § 2.4: what requirements it has, what entity it affects, with what approach, on which structure, with which operations, under which rules, with what safeguards.

At the end, Revision · canvas.md with the editor, Save changes, 🔄 Regenerate e ✅ Approve → go to Propose.

Rigenera it starts over from scratch and you lose your changes; if you have manually edited the text, save first or give up regeneration.

The Canvas is the document worth spending time on: the specification of phase 3 derives from it, and an approximate Canvas produces an approximate specification.

Limits of this chapter#

  • Drafts only live in your browser until you save on the server.
  • The interview conversation does not reload from the server: remains alone explore.md (§ 11.6).
  • The type of development is not changed halfway without invalidating the collected context.
  • Regeneration overwrites: save the manual changes first.
  • Explore and Canvas require the model. The dry-run no.
  • Features are not removed from the console. An abandoned amendment remains below changes/ until someone removes it from the filesystem.
  • The pipeline is not available in read-only mode (§ 4.7).

12. The Pipeline: Proposals, governance and execution#

The third phase transforms the Canvas into a verifiable specification and into a prompt ready for a code-writing agent. It is the densest phase, and the only one that can modify files on the disk.

12.1 Generate specification#

⚙️ Propose · BDD Specifications produce spec.md From the approved Canvas: scenarios in GIVEN/WHEN/THEN form, that is starting condition, action, expected result. It is a format that reads like prose but translates into test cases.

Generation takes minutes: "Generating specifications in progress via local LLM…".

At the end, Revision · spec.md with the notice 'Approve to unlock the final prompt,' the editor, Save changes, 🔄 Regenerate e ✅ Approve spec.md.

12.2 The open points#

Under the editor appears the report of the open points: the issues that the specification could not resolve, because the interview had not clarified them.

These are not system defects: they are the ambiguities you left, made explicit instead of buried in a vague sentence. A typical open point is 'the command to adjust the volume is not specified'.

As long as they remain undecided, the contract is not complete. They are not canceled: they are decided.

12.3 Governance validation#

The box 🛡️ Governance validation (pre-apply) check the Canvas + Spec pair, partly with deterministic rules and partly with the model. Valid canvas + spec avvia.

The link Review open points and associations opens the decision editor. For each point choose:

DecisioneQuando
I accept the gap and proceedThe matter remains open and you take responsibility for it
I record the resolutionThe issue has been resolved, and write as

Two fields are also needed: Declared name — and the console is honest on the label, «identity not verified»: it is a declared signature, not authenticated — and Motivation / resolution, where you write the reason. Then Record decision.

The motivation is the part that matters. In six months, when someone asks why the volume works that way, the answer is right there.

A single decision can cover an issue raised by the validation, and only if it is of the type accepted: if you try otherwise, the console warns «Only accepted can cover a relief».

When the semantic part is not available#

Validation consists of two checks, and they can have different outcomes. That strutturale It is deterministic: it checks the form of the contract and either passes or fails. That semantico it is entrusted to the model, and it may turn out unavailable — typically because the model's response is not interpretable, which happens more often with smaller local models.

In that case you will see the structural check passed and the semantic one declared unavailable. This is the correct behavior: not available does not mean surpassed, and the system prefers to say it instead of pretending to have checked.

The rest continues to work: the open points are still listed and the gate continues to block until you decide on them, with a message like 'Points without recorded decision: OP-001'. You can then record the decisions and proceed, knowing however that On the merit of the specific matter, no one has given an opinion: that check remains with you.

If you need semantic control, it's a matter of which model the installation uses, not how you use the console: see the administrator manual.

12.4 Comparison with the validated version#

Compare with the validated version shows side by side the current version and the one that had been validated.

It is necessary because the validation refers to a specific content. If after obtaining it you touch the Canvas or the Spec, the validation no longer applies to what you have in hand, and this comparison is the way to see exactly what has changed.

12.5 The final prompt#

The box 🚀 Final prompt for Claude Code / Cursor contains the text to pass to an agent who writes code, already complete with the necessary context.

Three commands:

  • 🧠 Agent Context — shows the context block with a value of confidence, that is, how solid the collected material is considered by the system. A low value is an invitation to go back, not to proceed faster.
  • ⬇️ Export JSON — download the contract in an editable form, to keep or pass on to other tools.
  • Copia — copy the prompt to the clipboard; the button becomes «Copied ✓».

12.6 Execute with an agent#

The box 🤖 Run with agent It allows an agent to work directly from here. Four controls:

This is the only console command that always requires an access key, even when you are working on the same server machine. It is a security choice: it is the only point from which files can be written, and simply having a page open in the browser is not enough to authorize it. If the installation does not have a configured key, by pressing Esegui The console asks you for it (§ 16.4) and execution does not start until you have a valid one. Obtaining it is the responsibility of the person managing the installation; the rest of the pipeline works without it.

Agente — The list is populated by the server, and an unavailable agent appears with the reason. Modello — 🧠 Sonnet, 🚀 Opus, ⚡ Haiku, with the usual compromise between capability, speed, and cost. Mode — see below. Tentativi — how many automatic retries in case of verification failure; active only in Agentic, because «only in Agentic mode» there is code written to be verified.

12.7 The three modes — to be read before pressing Run#

ModeWhat can he/she/it do
🔍 Suggest-only (read-only)He reads the project and proposes. He/She doesn't write anything.
⚡ Agentic (writes in the project)writes files to the disk, confined to the folder code/ of the project
💬 One-shot (no tool)just generate text, without accessing files

Agentic is the only mode that modifies your project. Before leaving, the console opens a red confirmation: «The Agentic mode writes files in the project. Continue?».

The perimeter is imposed by the system, not by the model's goodwill: writing outside of code/ is refused. However, the fact remains that inside code/ The files are actually modified. If the project is not under version control, make sure you can revert before confirming.

If you just want to see what it would do, use Suggest-only.

12.8 The Execution Console#

The box below the controls shows how it went. Two outcomes, very different.

If the gate does not authorize, the execution does not start at all, and instead a list of reasons appears, one per line, each with the solution.

The reasons that are encountered most often:

MotivoSignificatoWhat to do
open_points_unaddressedthere are open points without a decision, listed by identifierrecord its acceptance or reasoned resolution (§ 12.3)
validation_unavailableThe semantic validation was not successfulrepeat it; if it repeats, see § 12.3
unreviewed_corpus_changesdocuments changed after validationnon-blocking warning: it only reports that the relevance has not been reassessed

It is the intended behavior: the contract goes to an agent who writes code only if it is complete. It is worth reading the reasons instead of trying to find a way around them — they say exactly what is missing.

If the gate authorizes, the output flows in real time: the reasoning, the tools invoked, the final result.

In Agentic mode, at the end of the writing the server executes the verification commands — compilation, tests — taken from its own configuration and never from the model. If they fail and you have allowed more than one attempt, the agent tries again.

12.9 OR work outside#

Nothing obliges one to execute from here. Copia o ⬇️ Export JSON They bring the contract into your usual editor, with the same material.

It is convenient when the work is long and you want to follow it closely, when you use a tool that is not listed, or when you prefer the version control of your environment over the perimeter imposed by the console. The pipeline does not mind: phase 4 checks the actual code, no matter how it was written.

Limits of this chapter#

  • The name of the person who decides is not verified. It is a statement, not an authentication.
  • Validation ages: Any subsequent change to the contract makes it outdated.
  • The semantic part may be unavailable, and does not equate to a positive outcome (§ 12.3).
  • The Agentic mode really writes, and the interface does not have an undo.
