  • The available agents and their models depend on the installation: keys and permissions are not configured from here.
  • The verification after execution uses the commands configured on the server. If none have been defined, nothing is checked.
  • Generation, validation, and execution require the model and they are the slowest operations on the console.

13. The Pipeline: Drift and Archive#

The last two stages close the cycle: the fourth compares what you had promised with what was actually written, the fifth puts away the work and resets the index.

13.1 Step 4 — The misalignment check#

Il drift it is the distance between the contract — canvas.md e spec.md — and the code that exists on the disc. Run check He/she/it measures it.

The analysis is carried out by the local model and lasts minutes. The box 📊 Report Drift It fills up gradually: first it declares how many files it has taken on and in how many batches, then it analyzes.

The first lines are already informative, and it is worth reading them before the verdict: they say how many files were examined and how many were excluded. If the coverage is narrower than you expect — for example because the type of development restricts the scope to a single subfolder of code/ — the following report talks only about that portion, and an absence of divergences does not mean that the rest is aligned.

At the end, the box contains the list of detected discrepancies, each with the point of the contract to which it refers.

The divergences are divided into three families, and the correct answer is different for each one:

DivergenzaWhat to do
The code does meno of what was promisedmissing work: go back and write it
The code does diversamente as promiseddecide who is right. Often it is the code, because by writing it a constraint emerged that the Canvas ignored: then the contract is corrected, not the code
The code does moreeither it is a good addition to document, or it is out-of-scope work

The verification works regardless of the source of the code: written by the phase 3 agent, handwritten, or written elsewhere. It compares the contract with reality, not with history.

The button ➡️ Go to Archiving leads to the final stage. Do not press it until the report contains discrepancies that you intend to fix: archiving does not resolve them, it freezes them.

13.2 Step 5 — Archive#

Archiving moves the edit folder to changes/archive/ and rebuilds the entire index. From that moment, the modification becomes part of the project's memory: its decisions will be retrievable with a query, and will feed future Canvases.

The console states it without beating around the bush: 'Final operation and not reversible from the interface».

The button opens a red confirmation:

Archive the feature "…" and rebuild the RAG Graph? The folder will be moved to changes/archive/ and the operation is not reversible from the interface.

Before confirming, three questions:

  1. Is the drift relationship clean, or are the remaining differences consciously accepted?
  2. Do all open points have a decision with reasoning (§ 12.3)?
  3. The Canvas and the Spec describe what was actually done, not what was initially intended to be done?

If the answer to one is no, correct it first: after archiving, the correction is done on the filesystem.

13.3 What Happens#

The log scrolls in real time in the box ✅ Filing outcome: folder transfer, final review of the Canvas entrusted to the model, reconstruction of the graph and the index.

It is the reconstruction completa, non-incremental: it is the longest operation of the entire console. You can switch sections while it is in progress.

13.4 Notification of end of work#

Precisely because it is long, in the end it reaches a system notification of the browser. The first time the browser asks for permission; if you deny it, the notification still remains in the console.

13.5 Where the work ends#

After the archiving:

  • The documents of the modification are below changes/archive/ and, being indexed, they answer questions like any other document;
  • the final review of the Canvas feeds the panel Quality of the canvases of the Eval section (§ 14.5), which measures how accurately the contract described what was actually realized;
  • The lessons learned go into the material used to generate the subsequent Canvases.

This last point is the reason why it is worthwhile to also archive failed changes: a breached contract teaches more than a successful one, and the system reuses it.

Limits of this chapter#

  • Archiving cannot be undone from the interface. Reverting a change is an operation on the filesystem.
  • The verification of the misalignment is a judgment of the model, not a demonstration. It points out where to look; the assessment remains yours.
  • The complete reconstruction takes a long time and requires Qdrant to be on.
  • Drift requires the model.
  • It is not archived partially. The modification closes entirely.

Measuring quality#

Section Eval (/eval) answers a question that no other screen addresses: Are the answers getting better or worse? Two panels, two independent measurements.

14.1 What does it measure recall#

There is a set of test questions for which it is already known which documents should appear among the results. The recall It is the fraction of those expected that the system actually finds within the top results.

The metric in use — recall@1, recall@2, recall@10, depending on the installation — this page does not choose it: it is the one on which the automatic control is set, which decides whether a new index can go into service. The panel title shows it: if you read 'recall@2 over time,' the control looks at the first two results.

Attention to what non measure: it does not say whether the final answer is well written, nor whether it is correct. It measures only one thing, the ability to retrieve the right documents. However, this is the point where problems begin: if the source is not recovered, no quality of writing can make up for it.

14.2 The top four tabs#

SchedaWhat does he/she say?
current recallthe value of the last measurement, with below it the margin compared to the control threshold: green if above, red if below
andamento«uphill», «downhill» or «stable», and on how many evaluations
last evaluationthe date, the outcome and how many test cases
recall per kthe measurement calculated at different depths, with the one used for control highlighted

The last card has a hidden warning in the tip, and it deserves to be read: if the measure of control reaches 100%, the control stops distinguishing A worse version from a good one. A full score is not necessarily good news: it can mean that the test questions have become too easy.

14.3 The Chart#

With only one assessment, the graph is not there: in its place you find the sentence «At least 2 assessments are needed for a trend». It is not an error — an isolated measurement has no trend. The legend below is still visible and explains the symbols.

The horizontal axis is real time, not the sequence of measurements: two assessments on the same day are close together, one after a month is far away.

The dashed line is the soglia of the control, labeled with its value. The points stand out for shape rather than for color, so they remain readable even in black and white:

FormaLabel in the legendSignificato
cerchioeval-gate · promotion allowedthe version has entered into service
croceeval-gate · promotion blockedthe version has been discarded
triangoloeval outside the gate (manual or advisory)manual throw assessment, out of control
dashed linegate thresholdthe level below which a version is discarded

A cross corresponds exactly to the message 'Index built but not activated' of § 7.5.

14.4 The data in the table#

The collapsible voice Chart data in table report the same information in a readable and copyable form: Data, the measure, Esito, Casi, Versione e Commit.

It serves two purposes: to read the exact values instead of estimating them from the chart, and to link a drop to a precise version of the index.

14.5 The quality of canvas#

The second panel measures something different: not the retrieval of documents, but how faithfully the pipeline contracts described what was actually carried out.

It is powered by the revisions produced when archiving each change (§ 13.5). The status line indicates how many revisions there are and how the fidelity is distributed among them alto, medio e basso; below, a dotted pattern for modification.

The list Most frequent divergences it's the useful part: it collects the recurring deviations, with a count of the times they have occurred. A divergence that appears in five out of six changes is not an accident, it is a flaw in the method — information that the Canvas never asks for, or a technical constraint that always emerges too late.

As long as no changes have been archived, the panel says 'No canvas review yet: archive a change to populate the panel.' If, on the other hand, there are reviews but they have not detected any discrepancies, it reads 'No divergence recorded in the reviews' — which is a different outcome, and a good one.

14.6 When this page is empty#

It is the most common case in a new installation, and it is not a fault.

PannelloWhy is it emptyWhat populates it
recall over timeThere is no set of test questions for this corpus, and no evaluation has been carried outthe definition of test questions and the execution of the evaluation
quality of the canvasesno changes have been saved yetarchive at least one change (§ 13.2)

You can fill in the second one yourself, using the pipeline. The first no. Test queries are not defined from the console: they are a file that must be written and a procedure that must be executed outside the interface. It is the responsibility of the person who manages the installation, and it is documented in the administrator manual.

As long as that file is empty, the Console's «recall» tab (§ 8.8) remains at «—», and this is also correct: better no number than a made-up number.

14.7 Read-only#

The section does not exist: /eval responds 'page not found.' See § 4.7.

Limits of this chapter#

  • Recall does not measure the correctness of the answer, only the recovery of the sources.
  • The measure is worth as much as the test questions. A set that is too easy produces high and meaningless scores.
  • Test questions are neither defined nor executed from the console.
  • The fidelity of the canvases is a judgment of the model, not an objective measure.
  • The data is not being exported from the interface; the table is copied by hand.

15. The Integrated Guide#

La Guida (/infografica) is the only section in which nothing is done: you read. It explains how the system is built, in the language of those who designed it.

15.1 How to reach#

From the last item in the navigation, set apart on the right precisely because it is not a workplace, or with Alt + 6It also remains available in read-only mode and even with external services turned off: it is a static page.

15.2 The Inquiry Flow Diagram#

The heart of the page is the diagram «Selected project flow (POST /ask)», which follows a question from sending to response.

Read together with chapter 9, it clarifies something that can only be inferred from the Console: the path is not always the same. A structural question can be resolved directly from the graph, without a model — this is the outcome graph_answer from § 9.7 — while a content question goes from retrieval, to expansion on the graph, and finally to generation.

Understanding which path your question took almost always explains why it was fast or slow, and why it cited certain sources.

Below, sixteen numbered cards, each with a foldable in-depth section:

15.4 Guide or manual#

They answer different questions, and it's best not to confuse them.

GuidaThis manual
Answers tohow does it work?How do I use it?
Point of viewthe systemyour task
When neededwhen a behavior surprises you and you want to understand the reasonwhen you have to do something

The moment when the Guide truly pays off is when something doesn’t add up: a slower-than-usual response, an index built but not activated, a retrieval that pulls up an unexpected document. Cards 8, 10, and 2 explain those three cases better than any operational chapter.

Limits of this chapter#

  • The Guide describes the system, not your installation. Optional components may not be present on your machine.
  • It is not interactive: nothing it shows is clickable to real data.
  • The level is technical. The insights assume familiarity with the concepts of chapter 2.

16. When something doesn't work#

This chapter is in the form of a diagnosis: from the symptom to the cause, and to the thing to do. Where the action is not yours, it says so.

16.1 First aid table#

SintomoProbable causeWhat to do

In the bar there is a '... not reachable' badgeQdrant or Ollama do not respond§ 16.3
The browser asks for a keyThe console is on another machine, or you are starting an agent§ 16.4

Every question answers 'no results'the index does not exist or is emptycheck "Indexed sections" (§ 8.8); if it is zero, chap. 7
A newly uploaded document does not appear in the responsesapproved but not indexed§ 6.7 and chap. 7
‘Index created but not activated’The quality checks rejected the new version§ 16.8
Indexing ends in error§ 16.8
The response says that it cannot answerabstention, not fault§ 16.7
The preview of a document is empty or unreadablethe conversion produced little§ 5.4; refuses and recharges in a better format
Importing code copies nothingall files are in conflict or excluded§ 5.6
The pipeline job has disappearedlocal draft on another browser§ 11.3
The page remains on gray placeholder§ 16.5
/intake, /pipeline o /eval they say 'page not found'read-only installation§ 4.7

16.2 Buttons that do not start#

Some commands depend on an external service. If that service is down the button remains visible but does not start, and a notice explains why: «Qdrant not reachable: start it and try again».

It is a deliberate choice: a button that disappears makes one believe that the function does not exist.

ServizioIt is used for
Qdrantinterrogate, build the index, the semantic map
Ollamagenerate documents, refine, Canvas, Spec, drift, project brief

Il Dry-run The Canvas and the structural questions do not need Ollama.

16.3 What keeps working#

Con Ollama off: structural queries, graph map, Analysis, reading of documents under review, Guide.

Con Qdrant when turned off it drops much more: no quizzes, no semantic map, no indexing. Remaining are the reading of the staging, the pipeline in the textual parts, and the Guide.

Why a service is turned off, and how to turn it back on, is not the subject of this manual: report it to whoever administers the installation.

16.4 Requesting the key#

If the browser and the server are not on the same machine, the console asks for an access key. The message explains it:

This console requires an API key (VIBECRAFT_API_KEY of the server). This happens when the browser and the server are not on the same machine — for example with the Docker stack. The key remains in this browser.

Three things to know:

  • You don't invent the key: it is provided by the person who configured the server;
  • stay in your browser and it is not required for every operation;
  • if you get it wrong, the request does not repeat endlessly: the console tries once and then lets the error pass.

There is, however a provided exception, and it is not a malfunction: the command ▶ Execute of the block «Run with agent» (§ 12.6) requires the key sempre, even from localhost, because it is the only point in the console from which files are written. If the installation does not have one configured, that button cannot work: everything else does.

Outside of that case, if you work on the same machine as the server and the key is still requested from you, it is a signal to report to the administrator: it means that the console sees you as a remote client.

16.5 Uploads, Blanks and Errors#

Three different appearances, three different meanings.

The gray skeleton compare at the first loading of a section. If it lasts more than a few seconds, the server is slow or does not respond.

The empty states These are sentences, not blank pages: "Nothing in staging," "The answer will appear here after the first query," "Upload a feature to see the status of the files." They say that there is nothing ancora, and generally suggest the next step.

Error states they have a button Riprova. Press it once: many errors are temporary. If it is repeated, the detailed message is the information to report.

16.6 Notifications that do not disappear#

Information, confirmations, and alerts disappear after five seconds. Errors remain until you close them with ×, because they are often the only trace of the reason for a failure, and one looks elsewhere precisely when they appear.

Before closing an error, read it: afterwards you won't find it.

16.7 "He did not answer, and that is correct"#

The console refrains when the material is insufficient. In the tab JSON Response the outcome is abstained, and it is designed like this: better no answer than a made-up one.

When it happens, check in this order:

  1. Has the document been uploaded? Look in docs/ through the Intake.
  2. Has it been indexed? If the badge says 'to be updated', the document exists but is not yet queryable.
  3. Does the question use the words from the documents? Rephrase using the terms from the glossary.
  4. Are the parameters too tight? Increase the results to retrieve or the depth in the graph (§ 8.3).

If after all this the system continues to refrain, the most likely answer is that the information is not really there.

16.8 When the index does not update#

«Index built but not activated: quality checks not passed.» The new version was discarded because it would have worsened the recovery. The previous version remains in service, so the console keeps working. It's the guardrail that did its job, and it's worth understanding which newly added document lowered the measure: the Eval section (ch. 14) shows the drop.

«Index built but not loaded. Try again.» A hitch in the final step: repeat the update.

«Indexing interrupted.» The work has stopped. Repeat; if it happens again, report it.

Badge «Index error» or «Index to be reconstructed": use Rebuild index. If that's not enough, the index must be redone from scratch, and it is not an interface operation.

16.9 Where Your Range Ends#

These things non they are resolved from the console, and insisting wastes time:

ProblemaTo whom
Services down, server unreachableamministratore
Access keyamministratore
Read-only installationamministratore
Missing converters for scanned DOC, PPT, PDFamministratore
Model slow or unavailableamministratore
Definition of the test questions for the Eval sectionamministratore
Reverting to a previous version of the indexamministratore
Deletion of approved documentson the filesystem
Cancellation of a filingon the filesystem

When you report a problem, the information that really matters is three: what were you doing, the exact text of the message e the version of the index read in «Project status» (§ 8.8). For difficult cases, also the content of the form JSON Response (§ 9.9).

Appendix A — Glossary#

Each entry says what it is and where you encounter it in the interface.

Ambito → see Type of development.

Archiviazione — the closing of a modification: its folder moves to changes/archive/ and the index is rebuilt. It cannot be reversed from the interface. Pipeline, phase 5 — § 13.2.

Filing — the weight of a document in the ranking, which depends on its classification and its status. Explains why a less similar source can appear higher. Contribution 'A' in the Citations this turn — § 2.5.

Canvas — the document that organizes a modification according to the seven REASONS pillars. Pipeline, phase 2 — § 11.9.

Categoria — one of the six folders of docs/; determines the weight of the document. It is chosen upon approval. Intake — § 2.3.

Chunk → see Sezione.

Contratto — the Canvas + Spec pair considered as a single whole. The validation refers to a precise version of it. Pipeline, phase 3 — § 12.4.

Dev type → see Type of development.

Documento — a Markdown file in docs/, with governance metadata. It becomes queryable only after indexing. — § 2.3.

Bridge document — a document that links otherwise separate thematic groups; on the semantic map it has a white ring. Analisi — § 10.2.

Drift — the distance between the contract and the code actually written. Pipeline, phase 4 — § 13.1.

Amount — a domain term declared in the documents, which becomes a node of the graph. ENT Pillar — § 2.4.

Feature (or change) — a modification in progress, with a folder underneath changes/. Pipeline — § 11.2.

Gate — the check that decides whether a contract can be passed to an agent. Not to be confused with the quality control of the index. Pipeline — § 2.8.

Knowledge graph — the set of nodes (documents, sections, entities, code) and their relationships. Console, Graph Map tab — § 2.4.

Contents — the interrogable form of the documents. Without it, no question finds anything. — ch. 7.

Job — a long operation that runs in the background. — § 2.7.

Progetto — the separation unit: documents, code, and its own index. — § 2.2.

Open point — an unresolved issue in the specification, which requires a written and reasoned decision. Pipeline, phase 3 — § 12.2.

REASONS — the seven pillars that classify the nodes: Requirements, Entities, Approach, Structure, Operations, Norms, Safeguards. They determine the colors of the map. — § 2.4.

Recall — the fraction of expected documents that the system retrieves among the top results. It measures retrieval, not the correctness of the answer. Eval — § 14.1.

Sezione (or chunk) — the unit into which a document is divided for indexing: one per second-level title. It is what is retrieved and cited. — § 2.3.

Code symbol — a class, function, endpoint or table extracted from the files below code/ and connected to the documents that bind it. — § 2.4.

Spec — the specification with GIVEN/WHEN/THEN scenarios, generated by the Canvas. Pipeline, phase 3 — § 12.1.

Staging — the holding area where a document waits for review. Nothing goes in docs/ without going through it. Intake — § 6.1.

Stale (index 'to be updated') — the documents have changed since the last indexing. The answers remain valid but do not see the new material. — § 3.3.

Type of development — the subfolder of code/ on which a modification is imposed; it defines the writing perimeter of the agent. Pipeline — § 11.4.

Validazione — the checks, automatic and entrusted to the model, on the consistency of the contract. Pipeline, phase 3 — § 12.3.

Index version — a complete and unchanging construction. It enters into service only if it passes quality control; the previous one remains available. — § 7.4.

Scorciatoie#

TastiEffettoDove

← →previous / next tabConsole tab bar
Home / Endfirst / last tabConsole tab bar
← →move the separatorseparator between the two columns of the Console
Home / Endseparator at minimum / maximumas above
Tabnext elementovunque
Escchiudeconfirmation windows

Alt shortcuts also work while the cursor is inside a section, because the event is forwarded to the page framework. They cannot be remapped.

Navigate without a mouse#

The jump link. The first element reachable with Tab is 'Skip to content': normally invisible, it appears when it receives focus and skips the top bar.

The console cards They use the movable focus: only one element is in the tab order, and you move between them with the arrows. This is the expected behavior for those who use a screen reader.

The separator of the two columns can be reached with Tab and moved with the arrows: adjustment does not require dragging.

Confirmation windows They are real dialogues, not browser windows: they hold the fire and close with Esc.

Screen readers#

Areas that change on their own are announced: the state of the index, the state of services, the response progress badge, the results of imports and reviews. Notifications are also announced; error notifications remain on screen until they are closed.

The page declares Italian as the language, so the synthetic pronunciation is correct without any settings.

Reduced movement#

The Matrix theme has an animated character rain. If the operating system is set to reduce animations, the animation does not start.

The button 🌧 Rain on / 🌧 Rain off It allows you to decide regardless of that setting, in both directions: it is useful for those who have disabled Windows animations but want the animation here, and for those who want to stop it even if they have them enabled. The choice is remembered.

For prolonged reading the theme is convenient Classico, which has neither rain nor scan effect: it is also the one used for the images in this manual. Both themes are dark, so the choice does not concern brightness but the movement in the background.

Narrow screens#

The layout reorganizes below 1100, 800, and 480 pixels. All functions remain accessible. The two-panel screens — Console and Analysis — are inconvenient below 800 pixels, because the map and the detail panel can no longer be seen together.

Known limits#

  • Shortcuts cannot be remapped.
  • The graph maps and the semantic map are drawn on canvas: they cannot be navigated by keyboard nor read by a screen reader. The same information is, however, available in textual form — the list Citations this turn (§ 8.6), the list Relazioni of the Analysis (§ 10.5) and the card JSON Response (§ 9.8).
  • The chart in the Eval section has a complete textual equivalent in the entry Chart data in table (§ 14.4).

Appendix C — Known limits and boundaries of the manual#

What the console does not allow#

They are not defects: they are design choices, almost all aimed at preventing a careless gesture from damaging the corpus.

It can't be doneWhy, and what alternative is there
Change a project's id or move its folderonly the display name can be renamed; id and path stay fixed
Delete an approved documentApproval is the point of no return; removal is done on the filesystem
Overwrite an existing documentthe approval fails instead of overwriting; change the file name
Apply conflicting file in code importThe import is additive by choice; conflicts are resolved outside
Cancel a filingThe folder must be brought back on the filesystem
Revert to a previous version of the indexThe mechanism exists but is not exposed in the console
Query multiple projects togetherevery question lives within a project
Edit a document in stagingyou can refine it with the model or reject it; there is no editor
Define the test questions for the Eval sectionthey are written to a file, outside the interface
Review the questions already askedthere is no historian
Resuming the conversation of an interview already concludedthe server keeps explore.md, not the interview (§ 11.6)
Configure models, services, keys, roleseverything outside the interface

What the system does not guarantee#

  • Recovery is an estimate. The right source may not arrive first. Sources are always exposed so that you can check them.
  • The system can abstain, and it is the correct behavior when the material is not enough.
  • Document conversion is imperfect. A poorly scanned PDF produces poor text. The preview serves this purpose.
  • The spreadsheet formulas are not being recalculated: the stored value is read.
  • The judgments of the model are judgments, not measures: it applies to the fidelity of the canvases, to the verification of misalignment, and to semantic validation.
  • The arrangement of the graphs is not reproducible between two views.
  • The signing of decisions is not verified: it is a declared name.
  • There are no permissions for the user. Anyone who reaches the console sees all the registered projects.

Depends on installation#

Behaviors that vary from one car to another, and which, if absent, are not a usability problem:

  • availability of converters for scanned DOC, PPT, and PDF;
  • which agents and which models appear in phase 3 of the pipeline;
  • if the console is read-only (§ 4.7);
  • if an access key is requested (§ 16.4);
  • how many versions of the index remain available;
  • the quality control threshold on the index;
  • the very existence of the test questions in the Eval section.

The boundaries of this manual#

This is the manual of theconsole user. Are there others or are three more planned:

DocumentoCopreStato
Guided tourA real case followed from start to finish, with real data: what you get, why it's worthwhile, where it goes wrong. Designed for a presentation and for those who have to decide whether to adopt itdisponibile
Amministratoreinstallation, requirements, Docker, environment variables, rag_config.yaml, selection of models and providers, keys, roles, network exposure, backup, index versions, definition of test questions, updatesprevisto
IntegratoreHTTP endpoint, MCP server and its tools, command line usage, continuous integration hooks, measurement proceduresprevisto

The guided path it does not replace this manual and does not repeat it: shows a decision made on a specific case, where here you can find the full description of the checks.

In the meantime, that material exists in technical form: README.md for the installation, rag/README.md for the architecture, rag/SECURITY_SURFACE.md for the safety surface.

This manual compared to your console#

The images may be older than the interface you are looking at. When text and image diverge, the text is more reliable: the labels of the controls have been verified in the source code, the images are snapshots of a moment.

If you find a discrepancy, report it: this is the way this manual remains useful.
